deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is not by Riemann. It is in Dedekind's hand and is his draft of the 'Erläuterungen' to Riemann's Fragment XXVIII on limiting values of elliptic modular functions, published in Riemann's Werke (1876). Two features of the text show this. The writer speaks of a theorem 'den ich durch Verallgemeinerung des Abelschen Princips gefunden habe', citing Dirichlet's Zahlentheorie, 2nd ed., §143; that is Dedekind's own supplement. He also refers to 'der von Riemann angewendeten ... Methode' in the third person.

Setup from the previous page:
- α = e^{2πi/n}, with n > 0 and m coprime to n.
- The radial limit of log η(ω) as ω approaches the cusp m/n gives lim_{r→1} Σ a_ν/ν = (m,n)πi/(6n).
- Here a_ν = 1/(1−r^ν α^{mν}) − 1/(1−r^ν α^{−mν}).

Step 1 (convergence and continuity at r = 1). Dedekind's convergence theorem, a generalization of Abel's theorem, covers the case where partial sums are bounded uniformly in r. It gives (m,n)πi/(6n) = Σ_{ν≥1} a⁰_ν/ν. Here a⁰_ν is the value of a_ν at r = 1.
- [mine] Writing ζ = α^{mν}, one has a⁰_ν = (1+ζ)/(1−ζ) = i·cot(πmν/n).
- For ν ≡ 0 mod n we have a_ν ≡ 0 for every r < 1, so a⁰_n = 0.

Step 2 (reduction to a finite sum, Dirichlet's method from Crelle 19, §1). Two facts make this possible:
- a⁰ is periodic: a⁰_{ν+n} = a⁰_ν.
- a⁰_1 + … + a⁰_n = 0. [mine: the terms are odd under ν → n−ν, and a⁰_n = 0.]

Using 1/ν = ∫_0^1 x^{ν−1} dx and summing the geometric series in blocks of n gives
(m,n)πi/(6n) = ∫_0^1 f(x)/(1−x^n) dx/x, where f(x) = Σ_{ν=1}^n a⁰_ν x^ν.
Because f(1) = 0, the integrand is regular at x = 1.

Step 3 (partial fractions). [mine, details]
- 1/(1−x^n) = (1/n) Σ_ζ 1/(1−ζx), summed over all n-th roots of unity ζ.
- Since deg(f/x) < n, f(x)/(x(1−x^n)) = (1/n) Σ_ζ ζ f(ζ^{−1})/(1−ζx).
- ∫_0^1 dx/(1−ζx) = −log(1−ζ)/ζ.

Taking ζ = α^{mt} (which runs over all roots since gcd(m,n) = 1) gives
(m,n)πi/6 = −Σ_{t≢0} f(α^{−mt}) log(1−α^{mt}).
The t ≡ 0 term drops out because f(1) = 0. The principal branch is used.

Step 4 (imaginary part of the logarithm).
- 1−e^{iθ} = 2 sin(θ/2) e^{i(θ−π)/2}.
- Hence Im log(1−α^{mt}) = π((mt/n − 1/2)).
- Here ((x)) is Dedekind's notation for the representative of x mod 1 in (−1/2, 1/2).
- So ((x − 1/2)) = {x} − 1/2, which is the modern sawtooth ((x)) for non-integer x.

Step 5 (evaluating f at roots of unity).
- For ζ^n = 1, ζ ≠ 1: Σ_{σ=0}^{n−1} σ ζ^σ = n/(ζ−1). Hence 1/(1−ζ) = −(1/n) Σ σ ζ^σ.
- This gives a⁰_ν = (1/n) Σ_σ σ α^{−mνσ} − (1/n) Σ_σ σ α^{mνσ}. The formula is also valid for ν = n, where both sums equal (n−1)/2 and cancel.
- Use orthogonality: Σ_{ν=1}^n α^{mνk} equals n if k ≡ 0 mod n, and 0 otherwise.
- It follows that f(α^{−mt}) = |−t| − |t|, where |t| is the least non-negative residue of t mod n.

Step 6 (combining).
- [mine] f(α^{−mt}) is odd in t and log|1−α^{mt}| is even in t, so the real parts cancel.
- This leaves, on the next page: (m,n)/6 = Σ_t (|t| − |−t|)((mt/n − 1/2)) = 2n Σ_t ((t/n − 1/2))((mt/n − 1/2)).
- In modern notation: (m,n) = 12n·s(m,n), with s the Dedekind sum.

Purpose: an elementary closed form for the constant (m,n) in the behaviour of log η at the rational cusp m/n. This is the birth of Dedekind sums.
errors: No mathematical errors found; every step checks.

Minor implicit points: gcd(m,n) = 1 and n > 0 are assumed but not stated on this page; a⁰_n = 0 needs the remark that a_n ≡ 0 for r < 1 (the expression 1/(1−α^{mν}) is undefined at ν = n); the cancellation of the real parts of the logarithms is left tacit.

Evaluation of Σ_{ν≥1} c(ν)/ν for a periodic mean-zero c via ∫_0^1 x^{ν−1}dx and partial fractions
results.modern_name: Dirichlet's method for L(1,χ)-type sums / finite Fourier evaluation

results.modern_name: Dedekind sums; eta-multiplier constant via Dedekind sums

deep.surprise_reason: The page is in Dedekind's hand and is his draft of the published commentary in Riemann's Werke (1876), where Dedekind sums first appear. That is well known and credited to Dedekind, not to Riemann, so there is nothing new attributable to Riemann here.

transcription_corrections: The author is Dedekind, not Riemann ('den ich ... gefunden habe', and 'der von Riemann angewendeten ... Methode').

The insertion in 'und (wenn n ... vorausgesetzt wird)' is most likely 'positiv', in view of the next page's 'wie oben vorausgesetzt wurde, n positiv ist'; the transcription's '{+stets[?]+}' is doubtful.
The crossed-out matter before '6n' in the first displayed formula is cancelled and not part of the formula.
The cancelled additional term after Σ_{ν=1}^{n} a⁰_ν x^ν in the definition of f(x) is illegible and deleted; f(x) = Σ_{ν=1}^n a⁰_ν x^ν.
The final 'ist' at the bottom is a catchword continued on the next page ('ist,').
